A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MARKERGEN study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original sub-ability diagnostics, benchmark evaluations, component ablations and attention analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds pairwise quality comparisons, evaluations by additional judges, a human agreement study and expanded ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use external tokenization and counting, decaying marker insertion, and three-stage planning, generation and rewriting. Section 3's procedures and equations are retained. Appendix F supplies prompts for these existing stages without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both retain CNN/DailyMail, HANNA, TruthfulQA, HelloBench, GAOKAO and Ruler's TLG evaluation, including English/Chinese and precise/range length constraints. The added evaluations reuse existing generation tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds Gemini-2.0 Flash as the reference opponent for quality comparisons with MARKERGEN and Implicit in Table 9. Table 14 also includes a direct-generation reference in the expanded ablation. Existing Implicit and Ruler comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 supplements the original calibrated GPT-4o-mini scoring with AlpacaEval 2.0-style pairwise comparisons against Gemini, pointwise evaluation by three LLM judges, and human validation on 200 sampled comparisons (Appendix E.3). These substantially expand the evaluation design; original model sizes and sampling temperature remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 14 extends the original component ablation with isolated components, additional combinations such as insertion plus decoupling without planning, and relative costs. Appendix E.3 adds checks of judge dependence and human agreement. The residual-error and attention analyses already existed and are retained as E.5 and E.6.

E5.justification: Both versions state that each setting is run three times and averaged. v3 additionally reports variances alongside multi-judge means in Tables 10–13 and a human–judge Spearman correlation of 0.8794. No increase in repeated runs is documented.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results. v3 adds reference-model win rates, additional judge scores and aggregates, human agreement, and component/cost results in Tables 9–14. For example, Table 9 newly reports Qwen2.5-32B HANNA win rates against Gemini of 23.00% for MARKERGEN and 6.50% for Implicit.

T1.justification: The error decomposition, marker-insertion equations and length-bias regression model are unchanged. v3 writes out interval-membership formulas for the already-used Er and PM/FM metrics, providing explanation without new theoretical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: sub-ability diagnosis, tool-assisted explicit length modeling, three-stage generation, and generalizable length control while preserving text quality.

C2.justification: Appendix E.3 newly interprets human agreement and multi-judge results as supporting evaluation reliability and robustness. E.4 adds conclusions about component necessity and quality–cost tradeoffs. Existing mechanism explanations, residual-error interpretation and the open-source-only applicability limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix F provides representative TruthfulQA prompts for all three stages, including output formatting, length feedback and marker examples. v3 also explains existing evaluation metrics and repairs the missing prompt-appendix reference. The code-access disclosure remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Google (2024) Gemini-2.0 Flash reference for its new evaluations. Appendix A's related-work discussion and the paper's positioning against training-based and inference-based approaches are otherwise retained; AlpacaEval was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. Local edits standardize 'identifying error,' correct cross-references and explain metrics. v3 adds acknowledgments, two evaluation subsections and Appendix F, while renumbering the existing final appendix analyses.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displayed evidence with win-rate, multi-judge and component/cost tables (Tables 9–14), plus boxed prompt templates (Figures 14–16). Existing tables and attention plots are reflowed or relocated, the heatmaps are resized, and Table 7 receives a more informative caption.

improvement.justification: Supplying missing stage prompts improves reproducibility, while additional judges, human agreement and component controls strengthen the evaluation. The gain is limited by sparse human-study documentation and an overstatement of uniform quality improvements: Table 12 reports a three-judge mean of 4.27 for MARKERGEN versus 4.29 for Implicit on Qwen2.5-14B TruthfulQA.
